options.a: Seat whichever patient checked in first and ask the other to rebook
options.b: Review the schedule/documentation and escalate per office protocol
options.c: Have both patients wait while the provider decides who will be seen first
options.d: Apologize and see both by shortening each visit to fit into the one slot

distractorExplanations.a: First to check in ignores the actual booking record; the CMAA should verify the schedule before deciding who keeps the slot.
distractorExplanations.c: Schedule conflicts are an administrative task; the CMAA verifies the record and escalates to the office manager, not the treating provider.
distractorExplanations.d: Halving two visits to fit one slot compromises care for both patients; the conflict should be resolved by reviewing the schedule.

options.a: Using a cover sheet and sending the full chart so the recipient has context
options.b: Verifying numbers, using cover sheets, and placing machines in secure areas
options.c: Faxing to the recipient's main office number, then calling afterward to confirm
options.d: Including the diagnosis on the cover sheet so staff route it correctly

distractorExplanations.c: Confirming after transmission does not prevent misdirection to a shared main line; the number must be verified or preprogrammed before PHI is sent.
distractorExplanations.a: A cover sheet helps, but faxing the full chart violates minimum necessary, and the number still must be verified before sending.
distractorExplanations.d: The cover sheet should carry a confidentiality notice and contacts, not PHI such as a diagnosis that anyone near the machine can read.

options.a: The fixed dollar amount the patient pays at each office visit for covered care
options.b: The amount the patient pays before the plan begins paying covered services
options.c: The percentage of covered costs the patient pays after meeting the deductible
options.d: The monthly amount the patient pays to keep the insurance plan in force

distractorExplanations.a: A fixed amount paid at each visit is a copayment; the deductible is the total the patient pays before the plan starts paying.
distractorExplanations.c: A percentage paid after the deductible is coinsurance; the deductible itself is the amount paid before plan payments begin.
distractorExplanations.d: The monthly payment to keep coverage active is the premium, which is separate from the deductible and other cost-sharing.

options.a: A patient's plan requires a primary care referral before a specialist visit
options.b: A patient has more than one plan that may cover the same services
options.c: A patient's claim is split between the deductible and coinsurance
options.d: A patient changes plans mid-year and the old plan has already ended

distractorExplanations.a: Referral requirements are a gatekeeper rule of one plan (often an HMO); COB applies when two or more plans cover the patient.
distractorExplanations.c: Splitting a claim between deductible and coinsurance is cost-sharing within one plan, not coordination between multiple plans.
distractorExplanations.d: With no overlap in coverage there is nothing to coordinate; services after the change are simply billed to the new plan.

options.a: Follow federal/state timelines and procedures with tracking logs
options.b: Allow up to 90 days for any request, since HIPAA sets no deadline at all
options.c: Be completed the same day for every request, before identity is verified
options.d: Be set by the requester, who may demand release within 24 hours

distractorExplanations.b: HIPAA requires action on access requests within 30 days, with one 30-day extension; states may set shorter limits, never a 90-day default.
distractorExplanations.c: Identity and authority must be verified before any release; HIPAA does not require same-day turnaround, it sets a 30-day limit.
distractorExplanations.d: Requesters cannot set legal timelines; federal (30-day HIPAA) and state rules plus facility procedure govern turnaround.
